drivingQuestion: Does a grown woman have a virginity claim, given Rav's rule that she is given the first night?
outcomeNote: the answer follows in the next unit (ketubot.sugya091)

segments.he: וְהַבּוֹגֶרֶת אֵין לָהּ טַעֲנַת בְּתוּלִים. וְהָאָמַר רַב: בּוֹגֶרֶת, נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן!
segments.en: § The baraita stated: «A grown woman does not have a claim concerning virginity» because of changes as her body matures, her hymen is no longer completely intact. The Gemara asks: «But didn’t Rav say:» The Sages «give a grown» woman who had relations on her wedding night, «the» entire «first night,» during which she may have relations with her husband several times? Any blood seen during that night is attributed to the blood of her hymen, which is ritually pure, and not menstrual blood. Apparently, even a grown woman has her hymen intact.

moves.summary: Rav implies a grown woman has a hymen

edges.about: whether a grown woman retains her hymen and so is subject to a virginity claim

positions.claim: a grown woman has no virginity claim
a grown woman is given the whole first night (blood assumed hymenal)
